newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's rice buffer seen falling below target. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Manila's rice buffer seen falling below target. [CORRECTED 10:25 GMT]

text.p: The Philippines' rice stocks could fall below the 90-day level before July this year, agriculture officials said on Thursday.
The government has set 1.98 million tonnes, or stocks sufficient for three months, as the ideal level of rice buffer to be maintained.
But by July, the buffer could reach 1.12 million tonnes, or 860,000 tonnes below target, one official, who did not want to be named, told Reuters (corrects attribution.)
The official said the country may need to import between 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes during the lean months of July, August and September.
The Bureau of Agricultural Statistics said rice stocks at the beginning of the year reached 1.858 million tonnes.
It also forecast unmilled rice output at 4.991 million tonnes, equivalent to 3.244 tonnes of rice taking into account a 65 percent milling recovery rate.
Total available rice supply in the first six months is expected at 5.102 million tonnes as against demand of 3.982 million tonnes or at 22,000 tonnes per day for 181 days.
Escudero said the 90-day buffer supply was the ideal supply level before the lean months and said it need not be followed all the time.

An Agriculture official said an interagency committee that reviews the annual rice supply and demand situation in the country has proposed to Escudero to allow the importation of around 500,000 tonnes of rice before the onset of the third-quarter lean season.
"The proposal also stipulated that an additional importation of around 400,000 tonnes should be allowed immediately if there is still a shortage," the official who requested anonymity said.
The Philippines imported 900,000 tonnes of rice last year.
